claims.statement: A polynomial map F=(P,Q): A2_C -> A2_C with J(P,Q) in C* is étale.
claims.note: Jacobian criterion in characteristic zero.

claims.statement: P and Q are algebraically independent under the Keller hypothesis.
claims.note: A nonzero constant Jacobian makes dP,dQ independent.

claims.statement: Zariski Main factors a quasi-finite Keller map as A2 -> Y -> A2 with the first map open and the second finite, where Y is the normalization in the function-field extension.
claims.note: Primary-source audit required for the exact hypotheses and formulation.

claims.statement: A normal affine surface finite over the regular surface A2 is Cohen–Macaulay and, under the stated equidimensional hypotheses, finite flat.
claims.note: Audit miracle-flatness hypotheses and connectedness.

claims.statement: If the finite normalization has no boundary/branching, it is a finite étale cover of A2 and hence degree one.
claims.note: Uses triviality of connected finite étale covers of A2_C.

claims.statement: When the boundary divisors are the only complement of A2 in a normal affine normalization Y, their classes freely generate Cl(Y).
claims.note: The localization proof is recorded in Track A; audit singular and codimension-two assumptions.

claims.statement: At a smooth generic point of a boundary divisor of ramification index e, div(dP wedge dQ) has coefficient e-1.
claims.note: Local tame DVR computation u=t^e, v=s.

claims.statement: A global monogenic normalization C=B[theta] forces the field degree to be one.
claims.note: Issue #3 gives the noncircular argument: if O=B[theta], then Omega_{O/B}=O/(f'(theta))dtheta; source etaleness makes f'(theta) a unit of C[x,y], hence a nonzero constant, and minimality forces degree one. Mutable candidate; see research/issues/issue-3-unramified-index/THEOREM-PACKET.md.

claims.statement: A global finite relative complete-intersection presentation of the normalization forces finite étaleness and degree one.
claims.note: Relative Jacobian determinant becomes a source unit.

claims.statement: There are canonical commuting derivations D_P and D_Q dual to dP,dQ.
claims.note: Direct calculation.

claims.statement: If a finite locally free B-order M in the function field is stable under D_P and D_Q, then locally delta(G)=A^T G+GA and delta(det G)=2 Tr(A)det G; hence its discriminant ideal is stable under partial_P and partial_Q.
claims.note: Exact matrix proof in research/issue-4/stable-differential-order/MAIN.md. The issue #4 constructor review returned BLOCK for promotion; this remains a mutable candidate.

claims.statement: A nonzero ideal of C[P,Q] stable under both partial derivatives is the unit ideal.
claims.note: Minimal total-degree argument.

claims.statement: A finite locally free B-order in L stable under D_P and D_Q has unit discriminant, is finite étale and connected over A2_C, and therefore has degree one.
claims.note: Conditional implication only: no stable order is constructed. Issue #4 records a ramified-DVR no-lattice obstruction, and its self-review returned BLOCK for promotion.

claims.statement: The canonical Euler, hyperbolic, and affine Lie-algebra fields encode infinitesimal target symmetries on the source.
claims.note: Direct commutator calculations.

claims.statement: Local finiteness or algebraic integration of an appropriate canonical affine action would force invertibility.
claims.note: Issue #5 binds the G_m terminal case to Shaska, arXiv:2607.20210v1, Theorem 3.3, only after an actual nontrivial algebraic action on source and target and invariance of the source open are proved. Regularity alone is insufficient.

claims.statement: Every nontrivially G_m-equivariant planar Keller map is an automorphism for every sign pattern of the weights.
claims.note: Source-bound to T. Shaska, Graded Keller maps and the Jacobian Conjecture, arXiv:2607.20210v1; audit full hypotheses before use.

claims.statement: A commuting effective finite group of even order forces a planar étale map to be an automorphism.
claims.note: Attributed in the logs to Miyanishi; exact statement/source must be verified.

claims.statement: After deleting two generic coordinate fibers, the unit lattice is generated by p=P-alpha and q=Q-beta.
claims.note: Requires irreducibility/nonassociation audit for generic fibers.

claims.statement: If the intrinsic quasi-Albanese map to (G_m)^2 is finite, equality of character lattices forces degree one.
claims.note: Check connectedness and finite étale torus-cover classification.

claims.statement: For N=C[x,y]/D_Q(C[x,y]), D_P acts bijectively.
claims.note: Follows from exactness of the algebraic de Rham complex in the dP,dQ frame.

claims.statement: Vanishing of the puncture/Gauss–Manin module would force a surjective divergence-free derivation and then invertibility.
claims.note: Classification theorem and exact hypotheses need primary-source audit.

claims.statement: The exact symplectic identity dP wedge dQ=dx wedge dy implies P dQ + y dx is polynomially exact.
claims.note: Polynomial Poincare lemma.

claims.statement: For every boundary divisorial Laurent expansion of the polynomial primitive P dQ + y dx = dH, the logarithmic residue vanishes, while the exact coefficient equations permit nonzero higher principal parts.
claims.note: Issue #5, PRINCIPAL_PARTS.md §6. Zero residue is not pole elimination. Candidate only; the issue-specific review is a self-audit, not independent acceptance.

claims.statement: The basic smooth one-boundary Wright ring admits no homogeneous constant-bracket pair in the natural grading.
claims.note: The degree/divisibility argument is recorded in Track G.

claims.statement: A simultaneous graded-reduction theorem would close the smooth one-boundary route.
claims.note: Leading forms may be powers with coprime exponents and several valuations can conflict.

claims.statement: Every branch meridian in the nonproperness complement has at least one fixed affine sheet.
claims.note: Requires careful comparison of the finite normalization and original affine source.

claims.statement: If the connected monodromy image were abelian and every component meridian fixed a sheet, the cover would be trivial.
claims.note: Group-theoretic core is elementary; geometric generation by meridians must be checked.

claims.statement: The required monodromy of a counterexample must be genuinely nonabelian and supported by cusp/tangency data rather than a purely nodal divisor.
claims.note: Needs exact plane-curve-complement hypotheses.

claims.statement: For every finite set S of height-one primes of B, one integral primitive element generates the whole semilocal normalization algebra O_p over B_p for every p in S; in particular one element can be adapted simultaneously to all ramified height-one primes.
claims.note: Issue #3 theorem packet. The object is the whole semilocal algebra over each base prime, not separate factors. Mutable candidate after local adversarial review.

claims.statement: After ramified-prime adaptation, every remaining height-one component of the index module has an unramified generic point.
claims.note: Formal localization statement only; it implies neither vanishing nor monotonicity of the remaining support.

claims.statement: If one integral primitive element generates the normalization at every height-one base prime, then the normalization equals B[theta]; in a Keller normalization this forces [L:K]=1.
claims.note: Conditional R1/S2 globalization plus the noncircular monogenic degree-one argument. It does not assert existence of such an element.

claims.statement: The normalization is locally monogenic away from finitely many singular/corank-two values.
claims.note: Fiberwise embedding-dimension argument; audit global openness theorem.

claims.statement: If primitive elements exist on a Zariski cover of all Spec(B) and their transition functions are affine-linear, then Pic(B)=0 and H^1(Spec(B),O_B)=0 globalize them to one primitive element.
claims.note: Exact scope from issue #3. Do not infer this from a cover of a punctured base without extending the affine cocycle.

claims.statement: A primitive element generating every height-one localization generates the normal finite algebra globally.
claims.note: Exact contraction and denominator-ideal R1/S2 proof in the issue #3 theorem packet; mutable candidate.

claims.statement: A hypothetical counterexample has finite asymptotic values on generic coordinate fibers; no affine ramification alone does not imply finiteness.
claims.note: This is the recurring escape-at-infinity obstruction.

claims.statement: The three-dimensional announced counterexample is a marked-simple-root/linear-factor incidence map for binary cubics, with resultant normalization.
claims.note: Directly recoverable from the displayed formulas in the conversations.

claims.statement: The three-dimensional map is generically three-to-one and loses sheets on the cubic discriminant without finite critical points.
claims.note: Root/factor interpretation.

claims.statement: Multiple sheets do not imply a global deck symmetry on the original source.
claims.note: A non-Galois connected cover can have trivial deck group.

claims.statement: The literal marked-cubic mechanism does not by itself prove or disprove the planar case.
claims.note: It is inspiration, not authority for JC2.

claims.statement: The claim K_Y equals the reduced boundary merely from purity is invalid.
claims.note: Correct generic coefficient is e-1.

claims.statement: The claim that exactness of a top form forces its zero divisor to vanish is invalid.
claims.note: Exact forms can have nontrivial zero divisors.

claims.statement: The claim that multiple sheets force a global finite symmetry is invalid.
claims.note: Monodromy and deck symmetry are distinct.

claims.statement: The claim that the x-elimination cubic has a square discriminant without qualification is inaccurate.
claims.note: The discriminant is a distinguished factor times a square; see conversation archive.

claims.statement: Several numerical low-degree frontiers stated in the logs conflict and must not be used until a primary-source audit is complete.
claims.note: The logs variously name 5, 6, or 7 as the first open generic degree.

claims.statement: A characteristic-p/p-curvature route may convert the commuting frame into a finite-monodromy obstruction.
claims.note: No closed theorem in the logs.

claims.statement: An equivariant degeneration route would need a no-escape theorem preserving degree and boundary type.
claims.note: Current torus limits can become automorphisms or lose sheets.

claims.statement: The positive-weight Rees deformation satisfies J(Pcal,Qcal)=t^kappa, yields every staircase equation, and has no nonzero bracket terms above the resonant stair.
claims.note: Independent ACCEPT bound to candidate 96fc7ec34bd3b685a0edeae7ecd4404abab7e2f1; see governance/reviews/issue-17-defect4-independent-gpt56.md and the mainline freeze record.

claims.statement: Every nonzero resonant layer pair is an explicit weighted graded polynomial automorphism; one such pair exists because the resonant brackets sum to one.
claims.note: Independent ACCEPT bound to candidate 96fc7ec34bd3b685a0edeae7ecd4404abab7e2f1; see governance/reviews/issue-17-defect4-independent-gpt56.md and the mainline freeze record. The proof is internal and does not consume CLM-016.

claims.statement: A nonzero resonant pair touching a top weighted layer forces the full Keller map to be a polynomial automorphism.
claims.note: Independent ACCEPT bound to candidate 96fc7ec34bd3b685a0edeae7ecd4404abab7e2f1; see governance/reviews/issue-17-defect4-independent-gpt56.md and the mainline freeze record.

claims.statement: For any primitive positive weight, every planar Keller pair with grading defect kappa at most 3 is a polynomial automorphism.
claims.note: Independent ACCEPT bound to candidate 96fc7ec34bd3b685a0edeae7ecd4404abab7e2f1; see governance/reviews/issue-17-defect4-independent-gpt56.md and the mainline freeze record.

claims.statement: At grading defect 4, each interior resonance (1,3), (2,2), and (3,1) either admits exact strict target descent or contradicts weighted support and the earlier staircase equations.
claims.note: Independent ACCEPT bound to candidate 96fc7ec34bd3b685a0edeae7ecd4404abab7e2f1; see governance/reviews/issue-17-defect4-independent-gpt56.md and the mainline freeze record.

claims.statement: At a monogenic height-one normalization S=R[s] with minimal polynomial f, the lift of a target derivation V satisfies V~(s)=-V_B(f)(s)/f'(s); its complete principal part vanishes exactly when the numerator is divisible by the different.
claims.note: Issue #5, PRINCIPAL_PARTS.md §3.1–3.2. The formula tests the normalization only when R[s]=S in the finite flat lci neighborhood; otherwise use V~(S) subset S. Mutable candidate.

claims.statement: In characteristic zero, a target polynomial vector field lifts regularly to the normal finite surface Y iff it is logarithmic along every reduced ramified branch component; height-one regularity then extends across codimension-two singular points of Y.
claims.note: Issue #5, PRINCIPAL_PARTS.md §3.3 and §7. Candidate pending independent review.

claims.statement: The standard radial lift E=P D_P+Q D_Q is regular across every ramified divisor iff every irreducible reduced ramified branch component is a line through the target origin.
claims.note: Issue #5, PRINCIPAL_PARTS.md §4.1. This is a tangency criterion; it does not prove the actual Keller branch is radial.

claims.statement: The globally regular-lifting canonical combinations are exactly target logarithmic derivations along the reduced ramified branch divisor; a branch Hamiltonian always supplies one, while a nonzero affine-linear logarithmic field need not exist simultaneously at all components.
claims.note: Issue #5, PRINCIPAL_PARTS.md §4. A branch Hamiltonian need not be locally finite.

claims.statement: Regular extension of a canonical or logarithmic derivation does not by itself imply local finiteness, completeness, or algebraic G_a/G_m integration.
claims.note: Issue #5, PRINCIPAL_PARTS.md §8.5–§9. The cusp Hamiltonian supplies an explicit non-locally-finite mutation.

claims.statement: Produce from the Keller boundary data a nonzero locally finite logarithmic target field whose regular lift preserves the source open, or prove the radial tangency conditions directly; only then bind the resulting algebraic action to the exact equivariant Keller theorem.
claims.note: Smallest surviving issue #5 bridge. Regularity and zero residue do not supply integration.

claims.statement: There exists a connected smooth rational normal finite-flat rank-three B-algebra that is Zariski-locally monogenic on all of Spec(B), has squarefree tame branch with one unramified sheet over each generic branch point, and contains an open A2, but is not globally monogenic; its displayed open A2 is not étale over the target.
claims.note: Issue #3 scoped algebraic countermodel. It falsifies the generic moving-index bridge without modeling the specified étale Keller source.

claims.statement: For the Keller normalization, construct one integral trace-free section s with fixed-section index Fitt_0(O/B[s])=B, equivalently Phi(s) in C*; proving only that the universal coefficient/content ideal is B is insufficient.
claims.note: The rank-three issue #3 successor reduces this to a boundary-cube valuation identity constrained by an exact primitive-coordinate differential congruence. Moving unramified scalar collisions remain.

claims.statement: For any primitive positive weight w, a planar Keller pair with grading defect kappa_w at most 4 is a polynomial automorphism.
claims.note: Independent ACCEPT bound to candidate 96fc7ec34bd3b685a0edeae7ecd4404abab7e2f1; see governance/reviews/issue-17-defect4-independent-gpt56.md and the mainline freeze record. This does not cover defect at least 5, prove existence of a qualifying weight for an arbitrary Keller pair, or establish JC_2.

claims.statement: Construct a finite full B-lattice in L stable under both D_P and D_Q; its reflexive multiplier ring then gives the required finite locally free stable order.
claims.note: Issue #4 remains open. The source-reflexive-lattice packet proves that pair-stability is equivalent to height-one unramifiedness, that every finite divisorial source-pole stage escapes at ramification, and that multiplier closure is automatic. No finite pair-stable lattice is constructed.

claims.statement: Under the finite-locally-free rank-three hypothesis, trace splitting gives a free rank-two trace-zero module E, and Phi(s)=1 wedge s wedge s^2 is an intrinsic binary cubic whose fixed-section determinant gives the local generation, Fitting, and discriminant-index criteria.
claims.note: Rank-three issue #3 successor; Quillen-Suslin is source-bound and the finite-flat hypothesis is audited rather than inferred from normalization alone.

claims.statement: The universal binary-cubic coefficient/content ideal is frame-independent, is a zeroth Fitting ideal, and equals the ideal generated by all integral index values; however, its being B does not imply that one section has unit index.
claims.note: The issue #3 cubic uX^3+X^2Y+vY^3 has unit content but no unit value, so the universal-content shortcut is explicitly retired.

claims.statement: For a finite-locally-free rank-three Keller normalization, four fixed source-linear directions cover every cubic etale fiber away from the boundary image; together with one boundary-adapted integral section, their fixed-section index values have no common height-one factor.
claims.note: This is a finite gcd-one certificate, not one global primitive section; a generic combination can create a new collision divisor.

claims.statement: For any primitive cubic coordinate t with minimal polynomial F and quadratic representatives x=X(t), y=Y(t), the Keller identity is equivalent modulo F to F_T=F_T(X_PY_Q-X_QY_P)+F_P(X_QY_T-X_TY_Q)+F_Q(X_TY_P-X_PY_T).
claims.note: All coefficient derivatives hold T fixed; clearing coefficients exposes the boundary denominators. No principalization is inferred.

claims.statement: In a Keller normalization the relative different/ramification support is contained in Y minus the specified source open; this excludes the issue #3 countermodel's interior-different pattern, while leaving unramified scalar collision divisors possible.
claims.note: Fixed or affine-linear first-coordinate constant-Jacobian repairs of the displayed countermodel are triangular automorphisms; the deformation audit is not exhaustive.
